messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> PD-INC-8423: Private VPC egress connectivity failures detected for customer 'AtlasCo'. Alert source: private-controlplane / agent-heartbeat-loss. Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-INC-8423 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: Paging on-call: Alice Chen (sre-oncall) — escalation policy: private-vpc-ops.

Alice Chen: ack — I’m on it. pulling logs and index of affected agents. starting runbook: private-vpc/egress-failure.

Ben Kapoor: seeing high 5xx spikes from atlasco-prod in the last 2m, graph: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/atlasco/egress-errors?from=now-15m to now. roughly 40-60% request failures.

Alice Chen: confirmed. PD says agent heartbeat lost for atlas-01 and atlas-02. control plane reports failed NAT translations.

Samir Ram: tagging in network. can we get the agent host IPs?

Ben Kapoor: atlas-01 -> 10.12.34.7, atlas-02 -> 10.12.34.8. reachable via bastion. I can jump in.

Alice Chen: steps: 1) check agent process 2) check iptables/SNAT rules 3) check host egress routing table 4) if stuck, restart redwood-agent and control-plane connection.

Ben Kapoor: SSHed to atlas-01. redwood-agent process is running but logs show repeated: `ERROR kvcache: failed to open socket: no route to host`.

```
# tail -n 50 /var/log/redwood-agent.log
2026-03-14T02:00:11Z ERROR net: write tcp 10.12.34.7:43210->172.16.10.2:443: write: network is unreachable
2026-03-14T02:00:13Z WARN heartbeat: missed 3 checks
```

Ben Kapoor: ip route on host: ``ip route show table 100`` -> default via 10.12.99.1 dev eth0 scope link metric 100. But controlplane routes expect next-hop 10.12.98.1 (weird). looks like customer side eBGP change?

Maya Gupta: customer network team (AtlasCo) on slack says they pushed an eBGP filter change 2m ago for maintenance. They claim they reverted but we still see asymmetric route. Customer impact: their requests to our private endpoint are being blackholed at their edge.

Samir Ram: running `tcpdump -i eth0 host 172.16.10.2` — no controlplane packets leaving. Can we force the agent to rebind / re-establish session?

Alice Chen: try `sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent` on atlas-01, then atlas-02. Also trigger control plane resync for that customer: `rdctl private resync --customer atlasco --force`

Ben Kapoor: restarted atlas-01 agent. logs now show TLS handshake succeed -> `connected to controlplane`, kvcache warmup. issuing resync now.

Alice Chen: resync command returned: `queued resync for atlasco (2 agents)`.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-8423 updated: acknowledged by Alice Chen, note: "restarted agents + resync".

Ben Kapoor: traffic slowly returning. error rate down from 60% -> ~15% in 3 min. Grafana confirms success.

Maya Gupta: AtlasCo engineer: confirming they see successful connections and no packet drops now. They reverted the BGP change again and flushed their filters. They will monitor for 30m.

Alice Chen: marking incident as mitigated. Customer impact: majority of requests to AtlasCo private endpoint were failing for ~9 minutes between 02:00-02:09 UTC. No other customers impacted. Estimated user-facing errors: ~3k requests failed (customer reported rate-limited service).

Samir Ram: follow-up: need to add a control-plane guard for route-mismatch detection + alert when agent's default next-hop != expected next-hop for customer's VPC. Filing infra ticket.

Alice Chen: handing off to Ben Kapoor for overnight follow-up & RCA write-up. Ben — please confirm you've captured logs and evidence in PD and created ticket.

Ben Kapoor: On it. I'll attach logs, `ip route` outputs, and the agent logs to PD-INC-8423, and create GH issue in infra/private-networking repo referencing PD-INC-8423.

Alice Chen: thanks all. closing pager for now but keeping channel open for updates.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-8423 status -> resolved (mitigated).

Ben Kapoor: next steps (quick):
- GH: infra/private-networking #456 -> detect-route-mismatch
- Add runbook step to check customer BGP config before resync
- Schedule postmortem with AtlasCo POC

Alice Chen: noted. handoff done. :thumbsup:
